cumleler: How is the brain's tiny response to sound pulled out of noise?
The auditory brainstem response, or ABR, is usually under one microvolt.
Background brain and muscle activity is tens of microvolts.
The fix: repeat the stimulus thousands of times and average.
The response stays in place and is kept; random noise cancels out.
With two thousand sweeps, noise shrinks roughly forty-five times.
